title: Electricity and Magnetism
seo_title: Grade 11 Physics (SPH3U): Electricity and Magnetism Worksheets (Ontario)
standard_text: Electric current, potential difference and resistance; Ohm's law; series and parallel circuits and Kirchhoff's laws; electrical power and energy; magnetic fields, the motor principle, electromagnetic induction and transformers. key_sub: Series: currents equal, voltages add. Parallel: voltages equal, currents add.
body_html:
How to think about it

Current I = Q ÷ t (amperes); potential difference V = E ÷ Q (volts); resistance R = V ÷ I (ohms). In series, RT = R₁ + R₂ + …; in parallel, 1/RT = 1/R₁ + 1/R₂ + …. Kirchhoff: current in = current out at a junction; voltage gains = voltage drops around a loop.

A current makes a magnetic field (right-hand rule). A current-carrying wire in a magnetic field feels a force — the motor principle. A changing magnetic field induces a current (Faraday, Lenz). A transformer changes voltage: Vs/Vp = Ns/Np.

Example

A 12 V battery drives 0.50 A through a lamp. Resistance?

R = V ÷ I = 12 ÷ 0.50

Answer: 24 Ω

Example

Two 6 Ω resistors in parallel. Total resistance?

1/R = 1/6 + 1/6

Answer: 3 Ω

Common mistakes

  • Adding parallel resistances like series ones.
  • Thinking current is used up by a lamp: the same current leaves it.
  • Thinking a transformer works with direct current.

faq.q: Why are homes wired in parallel?
faq.a: Each device gets the full voltage and can be switched on or off without affecting the others.

sets.title: Magnetic fields and the motor principle

items.q: Is gold a magnetic material?
items.e: Iron, steel, nickel and cobalt are magnetic. Most other metals are not.

items.q: A wire carries a current to the left in a magnetic field that points down the page. Use Fleming's left-hand rule. In which direction is the force on the wire?
items.e: Left hand: First finger = Field (down the page), seCond finger = Current (to the left), thuMb = Motion/force (out of the page).

items.q: A wire 0.2 m long carries a current of 5 A at right angles to a magnetic field of 0.1 T. What is the force on the wire? (F = BIl)
A wire carries a current into the page in a magnetic field that points up the page. Use Fleming's left-hand rule. In which direction is the force on the wire?
items.e: Left hand: First finger = Field (up the page), seCond finger = Current (into the page), thuMb = Motion/force (to the right).

items.q: A wire carries a current out of the page in a magnetic field that points down the page. Use Fleming's left-hand rule. In which direction is the force on the wire?
items.e: Left hand: First finger = Field (down the page), seCond finger = Current (out of the page), thuMb = Motion/force (to the right).

items.q: You look at one end of a solenoid. The current flows counterclockwise around this end. What pole is this end?
c: no pole: the field is only inside
items.e: Clockwise current seen from an end makes it a south pole; counterclockwise makes it a north pole.

items.q: The south pole of one magnet is brought near the south pole of another. What happens?
items.e: Like poles repel; unlike poles attract.

items.q: A long straight wire carries a current into the page. Seen from the front, what is the direction of the magnetic field lines around the wire?
c: straight lines away from the wire
items.e: Right-hand grip rule: thumb along the current, curled fingers give the field direction (out of the page: counterclockwise).

items.q: A wire in a magnetic field pointing down the page feels a force into the page. Use Fleming's left-hand rule. In which direction is the current?
items.e: Left hand: First finger = Field, seCond finger = Current, thuMb = force. The current flows to the right.

items.e: Iron, steel, nickel and cobalt are magnetic. Most other metals are not.

items.q: A transformer has 2000 turns on the primary coil and 40000 turns on the secondary coil. The primary voltage is 240 V. What is the secondary voltage?
items.e: Vs ÷ Vp = Ns ÷ Np, so Vs = 240 × 40000 ÷ 2000 = 4800 V (a step-up transformer).

The S pole of a magnet is pushed into one end of a coil. What pole is induced at that end of the coil?
c: a south pole, so it repels the approaching magnet
a south pole, so it attracts the leaving magnet
a north pole, so it repels the approaching magnet
a north pole, so it attracts the leaving magnet
items.e: Lenz's law: the induced current always opposes the change that produces it, so work must be done to move the magnet.
